introduction_markdown:
**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - SECTION B: COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Choose Picture B and describe what it shows (cook, big pot, steam, plate).
2. The cousin Lumbi's situation after her father's job loss.
3. The idea and the small start (a junction near the technical college).
4. Difficulties and the habits that win customers (cleanliness, listening, kindness).
5. Success and the big pot.
6. The message of the picture: the dignity of work. A clear link with the picture is required.

**Model composition (529 words)**

Picture B shows a young cook standing behind an enormous round pot. Steam rises from the bubbling food, a plate rests on the rim, and the cook's face, bent over the pot, is serious and absorbed. When I looked at it, I thought at once of my cousin Lumbi, and I decided to tell her story.

Lumbi was nineteen when her father lost his job at the sawmill. She had passed her GCE Ordinary Level with good grades, but there was no money for the Advanced Level. For months she stayed at home, sweeping the compound and watching her mother count coins. One Sunday after church, she said quietly, "Mama, I can cook. Why don't I sell food?"

Her mother laughed sadly. "Who will buy food from a girl without a shop?" But Lumbi had thought carefully. Near the technical college there was a busy junction where students, motorcycle riders and drivers passed at noon, hungry and with little money. Nobody sold a cheap hot meal there. With three thousand francs borrowed from her aunt, she bought rice, tomatoes, onions and oil, and she borrowed a cooking stove and a small pot.

The first day was discouraging. She sold only twelve plates, and she carried the rest home. But she did not give up. She came back the next day, smiling, and she washed her hands, her plates and her table before every customer, as her teacher of home economics had taught her. She listened to what the students liked, and she added more fish and less pepper. Slowly, the news spread. "Go to Lumbi," people said. "Her food is hot, clean and cheap."

After six months, the queue at noon was longer than the one at the bank. Lumbi repaid her aunt, hired two girls from the neighbourhood and began to cook beans and plantains for breakfast as well. Customers who could not pay on the day were allowed to pay later, and not one of them forgot. When her father heard that the girl he had pitied was now feeding fifty people a day, he wept with pride and offered to carry the firewood himself.

At the end of the year she bought the great pot that you see in the picture. She told me that on the day it arrived, she stood in front of it for a long time, because it seemed to her to hold all her hopes. In that pot she cooked for the weddings and funerals of the whole district, and with the money she saved, she enrolled in evening classes to complete her Advanced Level studies.

Whenever I pass the junction now, I see her at work behind the steam, her sleeves rolled up, humming a song, and I remember the picture. It shows more than a cook and a pot. It shows the dignity of work, the courage of a young person who refused to wait for help, and the power of a small idea carried out with patience.

Lumbi often says that no honest work is shameful and that a pot, however big, is filled one spoonful at a time. I believe her, because I have tasted the soup.

**Marking grid (the paper prints the split of the 20 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | A relevant treatment of the topic as set, a clear introduction, paragraphs that each develop one idea, a logical order and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied sentence structures, precise vocabulary, suitable register and tone, good use of linking words, a convincing style |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing fewer than 500 or more than 550 words, or ignoring the topic's exact wording (for example listing points instead of telling a story, or giving only one side when asked 'Do you agree?').
2. A weak plan: a long introduction, paragraphs that repeat one idea, no conclusion; or a pre-prepared composition that does not fit the question (it earns no marks).
3. Writing a composition that has no visible link with the chosen picture, or describing both pictures: the paper requires a clear connection with ONE picture.
